title: Servius (+ Servius Danielis), Commentarii in Vergilii Aeneidem — Servius on the Aeneid; Сервий, «Комментарии к Энеиде». Proposed unit: commentary on Aeneid 6
author: Maurus Servius Honoratus; DServ additions largely from Aelius Donatus' lost commentary
size: Thilo–Hagen 3 vols (~1,900 pp., incl. Ecl./Georg.); est. 450k+ words. Aen. 6 est. 30–35k words (estimates)
edition: Thilo–Hagen, Leipzig 1878–1902 (public domain; scans on archive.org/sourcelibrary.org; Latin text on Perseus). Harvard Servius covers Aen. 1–5 only
ru_evidence: Only selected excerpts on Aen. 1, translated by N. A. Fedorov in «Энеида. С комментариями Сервия» (Лабиринт, 2001); ancientrome.ru/antlitr/servius/serv1.htm; ru.wikipedia lists nothing else
en_evidence: Book 4 only: McDonough, Prior & Stansbury (Bolchazy-Carducci 2002; BMCR 2005.03.16). An unedited 'rough' complete e-book (Authors of Mitologia.pt, 2024) is not scholarly
other_translations: No complete modern translation found (not verified for Italian/German partials)
value: The richest ancient Latin commentary: grammar, Roman religion and ritual, antiquarian lore, mythography, and fragments of lost authors (Varro, Cato). Aen. 6 covers eschatology, philosophy and ritual. Indispensable for Vergil scholars, historians of religion and Latinists
ai_feasibility: high — formulaic lemmatic prose. Risks: separating Servius from DServ layers, Greek quotations, textual variants
pilot_unit: Servius + DServ on Aen. 6 (est. 30–35k words); a first release could cover Aen. 6.1–263 (~10k words)
